title: Reading_Links.csv
note: Added 2026-09-20. Raw bytes via download_file_content (base64; the harness spooled the result to a file, which was parsed and decoded — no model-mediated transcription), re-hashed from disk; byte count equals the live Drive fileSize 1482152. 6,035 lines: header 'Source Drive ID,Source title,Reader key,Open reading copy,Copy kind,Context' plus the 6,034 source-to-copy links. No corpus-declared digest; the digest recorded is first computed here, so exact:false. The object has no drive/inventory.jsonl row and appears in drive/deltas/2026-09-18/CHANGED_SINCE_SNAPSHOT.jsonl with status NEW (created 2026-09-17T23:56:31.413Z, after the snapshot); it is absent from PATH_CHANGES.jsonl, so it has not moved. Row 8 of this manifest records the same object tree-only under an earlier lane's 300,000-byte store limit; that row is left exactly as written and this row is an addition, not a correction of it. The table is navigation: every 'Open reading copy' URL points at an owner-private Google Doc or Sheet, and the Copy kind / Context columns are the source's words about conversions, not review of anything they point to.

title: PUBLICATION_INDEX.jsonl (repository-authored metadata index; not a Drive object)
note: Added 2026-09-20. Not a mirror of any Drive object: 22 metadata-only rows written here from Drive get_file_metadata / search_files calls made on 2026-09-20 — the five publication folder ids, the START HERE Sheet, and the 16 files of 04_AUDIT_AND_EXCEPTIONS with sizes and creation times. The 392 reading copies appear as per-folder counts only and were never fetched. Two of the three copy-folder counts (30 and 86) were enumerated through the connector; 01_READING_VOLUMES was not enumerated and its 276 is the source's own figure, labelled as such in the row. The audit gap proposed drive/source_map/PUBLICATION_INDEX.jsonl, which is outside this lane's directory, so it is written here instead. Format: the 22 records are one JSON object per line, but the file opens with a six-line '#' preamble, so it is not valid NDJSON and json.loads on line 1 raises; a reader must skip lines beginning '#'. Until 2026-09-20 this row declared mimeType application/x-ndjson, which a strict parser would have believed. Nothing in this repository parses the file.
